lemma_split_regular_crossed.statement: Let k be any field and G a finite group. Let L = k^G be the product of |G| copies of k indexed by G, with G acting by right translation. Then L is a Galois G-algebra over k, and the crossed product algebra (L,G,1) is isomorphic to M_{|G|}(k). In particular, over a field of characteristic p>2, M_{p^2}(k) is a crossed product algebra for G = C_p x C_p.
lemma_split_regular_crossed.proof: Let n=|G|. Regard L=k^G as the k-algebra of all functions x:G→k. For σ∈G define α_σ(x)(g)=x(gσ) for all g∈G. Then α_σ is a k-algebra automorphism of L, and α_σ α_τ=α_{σ τ}, because α_σ(α_τ(x))(g)=α_τ(x)(gσ)=x(gστ)=α_{σ τ}(x)(g). Hence L is a G-algebra. The elements e_g∈L, given by e_g(h)=δ_{g,h}, are orthogonal idempotents and L=∏_{g∈G} k e_g, so L is commutative etale and dim_k L=n=|G|. If x∈L^G, then x(gσ)=x(g) for all g,σ; for arbitrary g,h choose σ=g^{-1}h, so x(h)=x(gσ)=x(g), hence x is constant. Constants are fixed, so L^G=k. Thus L is a Galois G-algebra. Now let A=(L,G,1)=⊕_{σ∈G} L u_σ, with u_1=1, u_σ u_τ=u_{σ τ}, and u_σ x=α_σ(x)u_σ. The constant function 1 is a normalized 2-cocycle. Define ρ:A→End_k(L) by ρ(∑_{σ∈G} x_σ u_σ)(y)=∑_{σ∈G} x_σ α_σ(y). It is k-linear. For monomials x u_σ and y u_τ, ρ((x u_σ)(y u_τ))(z)=ρ(x α_σ(y) u_{σ τ})(z)=x α_σ(y) α_{σ τ}(z), while ρ(x u_σ)ρ(y u_τ)(z)=ρ(x u_σ)(y α_τ(z))=x α_σ(y α_τ(z))=x α_σ(y) α_{σ τ}(z). Thus ρ is a k-algebra homomorphism. Using the basis e_g of L, identify End_k(L) with M_n(k). For g,h∈G put E_{g,h}=e_g u_{g^{-1}h} e_h∈A. For t∈G, ρ(E_{g,h})(e_t)=ρ(e_g)ρ(u_{g^{-1}h})ρ(e_h)(e_t). Since ρ(e_h)(e_t)=e_h e_t=δ_{h,t}e_h, this is zero if t≠h. If t=h, then α_{g^{-1}h}(e_h)(s)=e_h(s(g^{-1}h)) is 1 exactly when s=g, so α_{g^{-1}h}(e_h)=e_g, and therefore ρ(E_{g,h})(e_h)=e_g. Hence ρ(E_{g,h}) is the matrix unit sending e_h to e_g and killing all other e_t. The image of ρ therefore contains all n^2 matrix units, so ρ is surjective. Since dim_k A=n·dim_k L=n^2 and dim_k End_k(L)=n^2, ρ is an isomorphism. Equivalently, the inverse sends the matrix with entries a_{g,h} in the e_g basis to ∑_{g,h} a_{g,h} e_g u_{g^{-1}h} e_h. Thus (L,G,1)≅M_n(k). Finally take G=C_p x C_p. Then |G|=p^2, and the result gives (k^{C_p x C_p}, C_p x C_p, 1)≅M_{p^2}(k). Since 1 is a normalized 2-cocycle, this exhibits M_{p^2}(k) as a crossed product algebra for G. The characteristic hypothesis p>2 is not used in the construction, so the statement holds in particular over any field of characteristic p>2.

lemma_tensor_crossed.statement: Let k be a field. Let A_1=(L_1,G_1,c_1) and A_2=(L_2,G_2,c_2) be crossed product algebras over k. Suppose that, with G_1 acting on L_1 and trivially on L_2 and G_2 acting on L_2 and trivially on L_1, the tensor product L_1 tensor_k L_2 is a Galois (G_1 × G_2)-algebra over k. Then A_1 tensor_k A_2 is isomorphic to a crossed product algebra (L_1 tensor_k L_2, G_1 × G_2, c) for some 2-cocycle c:(G_1 × G_2)×(G_1 × G_2) → (L_1 tensor_k L_2)^×.
lemma_tensor_crossed.proof:
Proof. In this proof a 2-cocycle means a normalized twisted 2-cocycle: if L is a G-algebra, c:G×G→L^× satisfies c(1,g)=c(g,1)=1 and c(a,b)c(ab,d)=a(c(b,d))c(a,bd) for all a,b,d∈G. This is the identity forced by associativity in a crossed product. This is the convention under which the crossed product presentation is unital with u_1=1. If a different convention is used, one first passes to the equivalent normalized presentation; since the lemma is about isomorphism classes, and tensoring with isomorphisms preserves the isomorphism class of the tensor product, this preliminary normalization does not affect the result. Hence we may and do assume u_1=1 in A_1 and v_1=1 in A_2; the relations with one argument 1 then force c_1(1,g)=c_1(g,1)=1 and c_2(1,h)=c_2(h,1)=1, and c_1,c_2 satisfy the twisted cocycle identity.

Let u_g be the homogeneous basis element of A_1 and v_h the homogeneous basis element of A_2. Put L=L_1⊗_k L_2 and G=G_1×G_2, with (g,h) acting by (g,h)(x⊗y)=g(x)⊗h(y). By hypothesis L is a Galois G-algebra over k, so dim_k L=|G_1||G_2| and L^G=k. Set w_{(g,h)}=u_g⊗v_h in A=A_1⊗_k A_2. Since A_1=⊕_{g}L_1u_g and A_2=⊕_{h}L_2v_h, tensoring over k gives an L-vector space decomposition A=⊕_{(g,h)∈G}L w_{(g,h)}. The subalgebra L is the (1,1)-component. For x⊗y∈L, w_{(g,h)}(x⊗y)=(u_g⊗v_h)(x⊗y)=u_gx⊗v_hy=g(x)u_g⊗h(y)v_h=(g(x)⊗h(y))w_{(g,h)}=(g,h)(x⊗y)w_{(g,h)}. Define c:G×G→L^× by c((g,h),(g',h'))=c_1(g,g')⊗c_2(h,h'). This is a unit, with inverse c_1(g,g')^{-1}⊗c_2(h,h')^{-1}. For basis elements, w_{(g,h)}w_{(g',h')}=(u_g⊗v_h)(u_{g'}⊗v_{h'})=u_gu_{g'}⊗v_hv_{h'}=c_1(g,g')u_{gg'}⊗c_2(h,h')v_{hh'}=(c_1(g,g')⊗c_2(h,h'))(u_{gg'}⊗v_{hh'})=c((g,h),(g',h'))w_{(g,h)(g',h')}. The first relation was already checked on pure tensors and hence holds for all x∈L by linearity. Thus the elements w_{(g,h)} satisfy the two defining relations of the crossed product (L,G,c). It remains to check that c is a normalized twisted 2-cocycle. For a=(g,h), b=(g',h'), d=(g'',h'')∈G, we compute c(a,b)c(ab,d)=(c_1(g,g')⊗c_2(h,h'))(c_1(gg',g'')⊗c_2(hh',h''))=c_1(g,g')c_1(gg',g'')⊗c_2(h,h')c_2(hh',h''). On the other hand, a(c(b,d))c(a,bd)=((g,h)(c_1(g',g'')⊗c_2(h',h')))(c_1(g,g'g'')⊗c_2(h,h'h''))=(g(c_1(g',g''))⊗h(c_2(h',h'')))(c_1(g,g'g'')⊗c_2(h,h'h''))=g(c_1(g',g''))c_1(g,g'g'')⊗h(c_2(h',h''))c_2(h,h'h''). In this action term, g acts on the L_1-factor and h acts on the L_2-factor, the cross actions being trivial by hypothesis. Because c_1 is a twisted 2-cocycle for the G_1-action on L_1, it satisfies c_1(g,g')c_1(gg',g'')=g(c_1(g',g''))c_1(g,g'g''); because c_2 is a twisted 2-cocycle for the G_2-action on L_2, it satisfies c_2(h,h')c_2(hh',h'')=h(c_2(h',h''))c_2(h,h'h'). Therefore the first components of the two tensor products are equal and the second components are equal, so c(a,b)c(ab,d)=a(c(b,d))c(a,bd) for all a,b,d∈G. Normalization is also immediate: c((1,1),(g',h'))=c_1(1,g')⊗c_2(1,h')=1⊗1 and c((g,h),(1,1))=c_1(g,1)⊗c_2(h,1)=1⊗1. Now let B be the crossed product algebra (L,G,c), with homogeneous basis e_{(g,h)} and relations e_{(g,h)}x=(g,h)(x)e_{(g,h)}, e_{(g,h)}e_{(g',h')}=c((g,h),(g',h'))e_{(g,h)(g',h')}. The assignment x⊗y↦x⊗y on L and e_{(g,h)}↦w_{(g,h)} extends to a k-algebra homomorphism φ:B→A, by the universal property of the crossed product presentation, because the elements w_{(g,h)} satisfy exactly these relations. It is surjective, since A=⊕_{(g,h)∈G}Lw_{(g,h)}. To see that this decomposition is direct, note that u_g and v_h are units: u_gu_{g^{-1}}=c_1(g,g^{-1})u_1=c_1(g,g^{-1})1 and v_hv_{h^{-1}}=c_2(h,h^{-1})1, so multiplication by u_g (resp. v_h) is an isomorphism L_1→L_1u_g (resp. L_2→L_2v_h). Since A_1=⊕_{g}L_1u_g and A_2=⊕_{h}L_2v_h are finite direct sums, A=(⊕_{g}L_1u_g)⊗_k(⊕_{h}L_2v_h)=⊕_{g,h}(L_1u_g)⊗_k(L_2v_h), and each summand (L_1u_g)⊗_k(L_2v_h) is Lw_{(g,h)} via (a u_g)⊗(b v_h)=(a⊗b)w_{(g,h)}. Since L is a Galois G-algebra, dim_k L=|G|; hence dim_k A=|G|dim_k L=|G|^2. By definition, B=⊕_{(g,h)∈G}Le_{(g,h)}, so dim_k B=|G|dim_k L=|G|^2. Therefore φ is an isomorphism. Consequently A_1⊗_k A_2 is isomorphic to the crossed product algebra (L_1⊗_k L_2,G_1×G_2,c).

lemma_crossed_p2_implies_artin_schreier.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2 and let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p^2. If D is a crossed product algebra for some group G of order p^2, then D contains an element a not in k such that a^p - a lies in k.
lemma_crossed_p2_implies_artin_schreier.proof: Let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p^2 and suppose D is a G-crossed product for a group G with |G|=p^2. By ref_4(i), since D is a division algebra, D contains a maximal subfield L such that L/k is Galois and Gal(L/k) has order p^2. Identify Gamma = Gal(L/k) with G up to isomorphism. Since D has degree p^2, L is a maximal subfield of degree p^2 over k, and L is a subfield of D. We first show that Gamma has a normal subgroup H of order p. The center Z(Gamma) of the finite p-group Gamma is nontrivial by the class equation. Choose 1 != z in Z(Gamma). By Lagrange, z has order p or p^2. If z has order p, put h=z; if z has order p^2, put h=z^p. In either case h has order p and lies in Z(Gamma), so H=<h> is a central, hence normal, subgroup of Gamma of order p. Let K = L^H be the fixed field of H. By the finite Galois correspondence, [L:K]=|H|=p, and because H is normal in Gamma, K/k is Galois with group Gamma/H, which has order p. Hence [K:k]=[L:k]/[L:K]=p^2/p=p. Now apply ref_14(a) to the Galois extension K/k of degree p in characteristic p. There exists an element a in K such that K=k(a) and a^p-a=w for some w in k. Since [K:k]=p, a cannot lie in k. Finally, K is an intermediate field between k and L, and L is a subfield of D, so a in D. Thus D contains an element a not in k with a^p-a in k.

c3_no_artin_schreier_no_galois_maxfield.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2 and let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p^2. If D contains no element a not in k such that a^p - a lies in k, then D has no maximal subfield L of degree p^2 over k that is Galois over k with Galois group of order p^2.
c3_no_artin_schreier_no_galois_maxfield.proof: Suppose, toward a contradiction, that L is a maximal subfield of D with [L:k]=p^2 and L/k Galois with Galois group G of order p^2. We show that L must contain an element theta not in k with theta^p-theta in k. Let G=Gal(L/k). First, G has a subgroup H of order p. If G is cyclic, say G=<sigma>, then H=<sigma^p> has order p. If G is not cyclic, take any nonidentity element g in G; by Lagrange its order is p or p^2, and it cannot be p^2 because then g would generate G, so its order is p, and H=<g> has order p. Next, H is normal in G. Indeed, every group of order p^2 is abelian: the center Z(G) is nontrivial because G is a finite p-group, and if |Z(G)|=p then G/Z(G) is cyclic of order p, which would force G to be abelian, contradicting |Z(G)|=p; hence |Z(G)|=p^2 and G is abelian. Thus H is normal. By the Galois correspondence, K=L^H is a subfield of L with [K:k]=[G:H]=p, and since H is normal, K/k is Galois with Galois group G/H of order p. Applying ref_14(a) to the Galois extension K/k of degree p in characteristic p, there exists theta in K such that K=k(theta) and theta^p-theta=w for some w in k. Since [K:k]=p, theta is not in k, for if theta were in k then k(theta)=k. But K is contained in L and L is contained in D, so theta is an element of D, theta is not in k, and theta^p-theta=w lies in k. This contradicts the hypothesis on D. Therefore no such maximal subfield L exists.

lemma_galois_tensor_split_regular.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2. Let L/k be a Galois field extension with Galois group H of order p^i, where i is 0, 1, or 2 (i=0 means L=k and H is trivial). Let H' be a group of order p^(2-i). Let L' be the split regular H'-algebra over k, i.e. the product of p^(2-i) copies of k with the regular H'-action. Then L tensor_k L' is a Galois (H x H')-algebra over k, where H acts on L and trivially on L', and H' acts on L' and trivially on L.
lemma_galois_tensor_split_regular.proof: Let A = L tensor_k L' and G = H x H'. We prove that A is an etale k-algebra, that dim_k(A) = |G|, and that A^G = k. Since L/k is Galois with group H, we have [L:k] = |H| = p^i and L^H = k. Write L' = product_{a in H'} k, and let e_a be the idempotent which is 1 in the a-coordinate and 0 in all other coordinates. Use the standard right-translation action of H' on L': for h' in H' and x = (x_a)_{a in H'}, define (h' x)_a = x_{a h'}. This is a left action because (h1 h2) x = h1 (h2 x), and it is by k-algebra automorphisms because (h' (xy))_a = x_{a h'} y_{a h'}. It permutes the primitive idempotents e_a transitively: for any a,b, h'=b^{-1} a sends e_a to e_b. Define Phi: A -> product_{a in H'} L by Phi(l tensor x) = (l x_a)_{a in H'}, where x = (x_a) in product k. The inverse map is (y_a)_{a in H'} -> sum_{a in H'} y_a tensor e_a. Thus A is isomorphic, as a k-algebra, to a finite product of copies of the field L. Because L/k is Galois, L/k is separable, so each factor L is etale over k; a finite product of finite separable field extensions is etale over k. Hence A is etale over k. Moreover dim_k(A) = |H'| [L:k] = p^(2-i) p^i = p^2 = |H| |H'| = |G|. For (h,h') in G define the action by (h,h') sends l tensor x to h(l) tensor h'(x). Since h and h' are k-automorphisms of L and L', this is a k-algebra automorphism of A. It is a group action: (h,h') after (h1,h1') is (h h1, h' h1'). The subgroups H x 1 and 1 x H' commute and generate G. Write A^H for the invariants under H x 1 and A^{H'} for the invariants under 1 x H'. Under Phi, the action of 1 x H' is given by (h' y)_a = y_{a h'} for y=(y_a); in particular it is the right regular permutation of the index set H'. If (y_a)_{a in H'} is fixed by 1 x H', then y_{a h'} = y_a for all a in H' and h' in H'. For any a,b in H', choose h' = a^{-1} b; then y_b = y_{a h'} = y_a. Therefore A^{H'} is the diagonal copy of L in product_{a in H'} L. On this diagonal copy, H x 1 acts diagonally: h sends (l,...,l) to (h(l),...,h(l)). Hence the H-invariants in A^{H'} are exactly { (lambda,...,lambda) : lambda in L^H } = { (lambda,...,lambda) : lambda in k }, because L^H = k. Since G is generated by H x 1 and 1 x H', an element of A is fixed by G if and only if it is fixed by both subgroups, so A^G is the intersection of A^H and A^{H'}, namely the diagonal copy of k. The diagonal copy of k is naturally identified with k, and it is fixed by G because both actions are k-linear. Thus A^G = k. We have shown that A is an etale k-algebra of dimension |G| with a G-action by k-automorphisms and fixed subalgebra k. By the definition, A is a Galois G-algebra over k. The argument also covers the edge cases: if i=0 then H is trivial and L=k; if i=2 then H' is trivial and L'=k; if i=1 both groups have order p. When H' is trivial the product has one factor, and when H is trivial the H-invariant condition is automatic, so the same proof applies.

crossed_csa_artin_schreier.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2. If A is a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2 and A is a crossed product algebra for some group G of order p^2, then A contains an element a not in k such that a^p - a lies in k.
crossed_csa_artin_schreier.proof: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2 and let A be a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2 that is a crossed product for a group G of order p^2. By ref_4, A contains a commutative subalgebra L of k-dimension p^2 that is a G-Galois algebra over k. We will find the required element inside L. Apply ref_2(i) to L. Let e_1 be a primitive idempotent of L and let H be its stabilizer in G. Then M = L e_1 is a field, H acts faithfully on M, M/k is Galois with group H, m = [G:H], and L is isomorphic as a k-algebra to M^m; in particular L is a field if and only if m=1. If m>1, then e_1 is a nontrivial idempotent, e_1 != 0 and e_1 != 1. Since e_1^2 = e_1, induction gives e_1^p = e_1, hence e_1^p - e_1 = 0, which lies in k. Also e_1 is not in k: if e_1 = lambda 1_L for some lambda in k, then lambda^2 = lambda, so lambda is 0 or 1, contradicting that e_1 is nontrivial. Thus a = e_1 has the required property. Now suppose m=1, so L is a field. Then by ref_2(i), L/k is a Galois field extension with Galois group G. Since G is a finite p-group of order p^2, its center Z(G) is nontrivial: conjugation on G has orbits of p-power size, and the fixed points are Z(G), so |Z(G)| is divisible by p. Choose an element of order p in Z(G) and let K be the subgroup it generates. Then K has order p and is normal in G. Let F = L^K be the fixed field of K. Since K is contained in G, k = L^G is contained in F. By the Galois correspondence, F/k is Galois with group G/K, so [F:k] = p. By ref_14(a), every Galois extension of k of degree p is Artin-Schreier: there exists theta in F such that theta^p - theta = w for some w in k, with w not in wp(k), and F = k(theta). In particular theta is not in k, because if theta were in k then w would lie in wp(k). Since F is a subfield of L and L is a subalgebra of A, theta is an element of A. Taking a = theta gives a not in k and a^p - a = w in k. This completes the proof in both cases.

lemma_reduce_p2_from_div.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2 and let A be a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2. Let D be the division k-algebra Brauer equivalent to A, so A is isomorphic to D tensor M_m(k) and deg D = p^e with e in {0,1,2}. If D is a crossed product algebra for a group H of order deg D, with the trivial group when D=k, then A is a crossed product algebra for a group G of order p^2.
lemma_reduce_p2_from_div.proof: Let d = deg D = p^e. Since A is isomorphic to D tensor_k M_m(k), we have dim_k A = dim_k D * dim_k M_m(k) = d^2 m^2. Because deg A = p^2, dim_k A = p^4, so d^2 m^2 = p^4 and hence dm = p^2. As d = p^e, it follows that m = p^{2-e}. Choose a group K of order m: K is trivial if m = 1, cyclic of order p if m = p, and C_p x C_p if m = p^2. Put G = H x K, identifying H with H x {1}. Then |G| = |H| |K| = p^e p^{2-e} = p^2, H is a subgroup of G, and [G:H] = p^{2-e} = m. The map D tensor_k M_m(k) -> M_m(D) sending d_0 tensor (a_ij) to (d_0 a_ij) is a k-algebra isomorphism, so A is isomorphic to M_m(D) = M_{[G:H]}(D). If e = 2, then m = 1 and A is isomorphic to D; since D is an H-crossed product and |H| = p^2, A is a crossed product for G = H. If e = 1, then D is an H-crossed product and H is a subgroup of G; by ref_4(iv), M_{[G:H]}(D) is a G-crossed product, so A is a G-crossed product. If e = 0, then D = k and A = M_{p^2}(k); by ref_4(iii), M_{p^2}(k) is a G-crossed product for every group G of order p^2, in particular for the group G = K chosen above. Thus in all cases A is a crossed product algebra for a group G of order p^2.

no_artin_schreier_no_crossed_p2.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2 and let A be a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2. If A contains no element a not in k such that a^p - a lies in k, then A is not isomorphic to a crossed product algebra (L,G,c) for any group G of order p^2.
no_artin_schreier_no_crossed_p2.proof: Proof. We follow the fix suggested in the feedback: we do not transport the crossed-product structure to A and we do not verify any cocycle identity on A. Suppose, for contradiction, that A is isomorphic as a k-algebra to a crossed product algebra B = (L,G,c) for some group G of order p^2. Let phi: A -> B be a k-algebra isomorphism. Since A is a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2, B is also a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2. Indeed, dim_k B = dim_k A = (p^2)^2 = p^4, simplicity is preserved under isomorphism, and Z(B) = phi(Z(A)) = phi(k) = k. The hypothesis char(k) = p > 2 is exactly the hypothesis required by the proved lemma crossed_csa_artin_schreier. Applying crossed_csa_artin_schreier to B, there exists an element b in B such that b is not in k and b^p - b lies in k. Define a = phi^{-1}(b). If a were in k, then b = phi(a) would lie in phi(k) = k, contradicting the fact that b is not in k. Hence a is not in k. Moreover, a^p - a = phi^{-1}(b)^p - phi^{-1}(b) = phi^{-1}(b^p) - phi^{-1}(b) = phi^{-1}(b^p - b). Since b^p - b lies in k and phi^{-1}(k) = k, we obtain a^p - a in k. Thus A contains an element a not in k such that a^p - a lies in k, contradicting the hypothesis. Therefore A is not isomorphic to a crossed product algebra (L,G,c) for any group G of order p^2. QED.

lemma_cyclic_norm_quotient_exponent_divi.statement: Let k be a field, let L/k be a cyclic field extension of degree n, and let N_{L/k}: L^* -> k^* be the norm map. Then the quotient group k^*/N_{L/k}(L^*) has exponent dividing n. Equivalently, for every a in k^*, (a N_{L/k}(L^*))^n = N_{L/k}(L^*). In particular, if b in k^* has order e in k^*/N_{L/k}(L^*), then e divides n.
lemma_cyclic_norm_quotient_exponent_divi.proof: Let N denote the field norm N_{L/k}, and let H = N(L^*) be its image in k^*. We must show that in the quotient group k^*/H, every element has nth power equal to the identity. Let a in k^*. Regard a as an element of L^*. Choose a k-basis e_1,...,e_n of L, where n = [L:k]. The k-linear map m_a : L -> L given by m_a(x) = a x has matrix a I_n in the basis e_1,...,e_n. Hence det(m_a) = a^n. By the determinant definition of the field norm, N(a) = a^n. Since a in L^*, N(a) lies in H, so a^n H = N(a) H = H. In the quotient group k^*/H, the class of a is aH, and (aH)^n = a^n H = H, the identity element. Therefore every element of k^*/H has nth power equal to the identity, so the exponent of k^*/H divides n. Now suppose b in k^* has order e in k^*/H. From the preceding paragraph, (bH)^n = H. Write n = qe + r with 0 <= r < e. Then H = (bH)^n = (bH)^r. By minimality of e as the order of bH, this forces r = 0. Hence e divides n. The case n = 1 is included: then L = k, N is the identity map, H = k^*, and the quotient is trivial. The cyclicity of L/k is not used; the argument holds for every finite field extension L/k of degree n.

as_compatibility_crossed_product.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2, let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p^2, and let K/k be a cyclic subfield of D of degree p. Let sigma be a generator of Gal(K/k), let C_D(K) be the centralizer of K in D, and let w_p(K) = {x^p - x : x in K}. Suppose u in C_D(K) and b = u^p - u in K with b not in w_p(K). If there exist lambda in F_p^× and x in K such that sigma(b) = lambda b + x^p - x, then K(u)/k is a Galois extension of degree p^2. Consequently, K(u) is a Galois maximal subfield of D, and D is a crossed product algebra for some group of order p^2.
as_compatibility_crossed_product.proof: Since D is a central division algebra, it is central simple of degree p^2. Let L=K(u). Since u lies in C_D(K), the elements of K commute with u. The element u satisfies f(T)=T^p-T-b over K; in particular u is algebraic over K, and because it commutes with K, L=K(u) is a field. Because b is not in wp(K), f has no root in K, so u is not in K. The roots of f are u+a for a in F_p, and all of them lie in K(u). Since f'=-1, f is separable, so K(u) is the splitting field of f over K and K(u)/K is Galois. Every K-automorphism of K(u) sends u to another root of f, hence to u+a for some a in F_p; thus Gal(K(u)/K) is a subgroup of the additive group F_p. It is nontrivial because u is not in K, so it has order p. Hence [L:K]=p, f is the minimal polynomial of u over K, and L=K(u) is a field. Therefore [L:k]=p[K:k]=p^2. For c in F_p, the K-automorphism tau_c sending u to u+c is well-defined; these are exactly the elements of Gal(L/K). Now set v=lambda u+x. Since lambda in F_p, v^p-v=lambda(u^p-u)+(x^p-x)=lambda b+x^p-x=sigma(b). Thus v is a root of f^sigma(T)=T^p-T-sigma(b), where sigma acts coefficientwise. Because f is irreducible, f^sigma is irreducible, so f^sigma is the minimal polynomial of v over K. Define a k-algebra homomorphism Psi:K[T]->L by Psi(a(T))=sigma(a)(v). Since f^sigma(v)=0, the ideal (f) is contained in ker(Psi); if Psi(a(T))=0, then sigma(a)(v)=0, so f^sigma divides sigma(a), hence f divides a. Thus ker(Psi)=(f), and Psi factors through L=K[T]/(f) to an injective k-algebra homomorphism phi:L->L. Finite dimension over k makes phi surjective, so phi is a k-automorphism of L extending sigma. For i=0,...,p-1 and c in F_p, the maps tau_c phi^i are k-automorphisms of L. They are distinct: restricting to K gives sigma^i, so i is determined; after composing with the inverse of phi^i, equality forces tau_c=tau_{c'}, hence c=c'. Hence Aut_k(L) contains at least p^2 elements. Since [L:k]=p^2, Aut_k(L) has at most p^2 elements, so it has exactly p^2 elements. The extension L/k is separable, because K/k is cyclic and L/K is generated by a root of T^p-T-b, whose derivative is -1. A finite separable extension whose number of k-automorphisms equals its degree is Galois; hence L/k is Galois of degree p^2. By ref_1, C_D(L) is a central simple L-algebra of degree deg(D)/[L:k]=1, so C_D(L)=L; thus L is a maximal subfield of D. Let G=Gal(L/k). Then |G|=p^2 and L is a G-Galois k-algebra. By ref_3, D is isomorphic to a crossed product (L,G,c) for some normalized 2-cocycle c. Thus D is a crossed product algebra for a group of order p^2.

lemma_pcentral_field_degree.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>0 and let D be a central division k-algebra. Let x in D not in k be such that x^p is in k. Then k(x) is a field of degree p over k. In particular, the polynomial T^p - x^p in k[T] is irreducible.
lemma_pcentral_field_degree.proof: Let b = x^p in k. Since x not in k and 0 in k, x is nonzero; hence b is nonzero. The subalgebra R = k[x] is generated by x over the center k, so it is commutative. Because x^p = b, every power of x reduces to a linear combination of 1, x, ..., x^{p-1}, so R is finite dimensional over k. D is a division ring, hence has no zero divisors: if a, c in D are nonzero and ac=0, then c=a^{-1}0=0. Therefore R is a domain. For any nonzero r in R, the k-linear map m_r: R -> R, y -> ry, is injective, since R is a domain; since R is finite dimensional over k, m_r is surjective, so there exists s in R with rs=1. Thus R is a field, and k(x)=R. It remains to compute [k(x):k]. The minimal polynomial m_x(T) of x over k divides T^p - b. First b not in k^p: if b = c^p for some c in k, then (x-c)^p = x^p - c^p = 0 in D, because x commutes with c and the binomial coefficients are divisible by p. A division ring has no nonzero nilpotents, since a nonzero element is a unit, so x-c=0, i.e. x=c in k, contradiction. Now suppose T^p - b were reducible in k[T]. Then T^p - b = f g with nonconstant f, g in k[T]. Let alpha be a root in an algebraic closure of k, so alpha^p = b; in characteristic p, T^p - b = (T - alpha)^p. Since f divides (T - alpha)^p, every root of f is alpha. Let m = deg f, so 1 <= m <= p-1, and let lambda be the leading coefficient of f. Then f(T) = lambda (T - alpha)^m in the algebraic closure. Comparing the coefficient of T^{m-1} gives -m lambda alpha in k. Since 1 <= m <= p-1, m is invertible in k, and lambda is nonzero, so alpha in k. Then b = alpha^p in k^p, contradiction. Hence T^p - b is irreducible. Therefore m_x(T) = T^p - b and [k(x):k] = deg m_x = p. Since b = x^p, this proves that k(x) is a field of degree p over k and that T^p - x^p is irreducible in k[T].

lemma_pcentral_centralizer_degree.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>0 and let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p^2. Let K be a subfield of D that is purely inseparable of degree p over k (for example K=k(x) for some x in D not in k with x^p in k). Then the centralizer C_D(K) is a central division K-algebra of degree p, equivalently dim_K C_D(K)=p^2 and C_D(K) has no zero divisors.
lemma_pcentral_centralizer_degree.proof: Let C = C_D(K) = { c in D : ck = kc for all k in K }. Since D is a central division k-algebra, it is a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2, and K is a simple k-subalgebra (a field) of degree p. By ref_1, the double centralizer theorem, C is a central simple K-algebra of degree deg(D)/[K:k] = p^2/p = p, so dim_K C = p^2. The same theorem gives C_D(C) = K; since K is contained in C, the center of C is C intersect C_D(C) = K, confirming that C is central over K. It remains to show that C is a division algebra. If a and b are nonzero elements of C, then they are nonzero in D, and because D is a division ring, ab is nonzero; hence C has no zero divisors. For any nonzero a in C, since K is central in C, the map L_a : C -> C, x -> ax, is K-linear and injective, because L_a(x)=0 implies ax=0 and therefore x=0. As C is finite dimensional over K, L_a is surjective. Thus there exists b in C with ab = 1. The identity L_a L_b = id_C shows that L_b is a right inverse of L_a; because L_a is bijective, L_b = L_a^{-1}, so also L_b L_a = id_C, i.e. ba = 1. Hence a is invertible in C. Since a was arbitrary, every nonzero element of C is invertible, so C is a division K-algebra. Therefore C_D(K) is a central division K-algebra of degree p, equivalently dim_K C_D(K)=p^2 and C_D(K) has no zero divisors.

lemma_as_element_centralizer_csa.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2 and let A be a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2. Suppose that a in A satisfies a not in k and a^p - a = b for some b in k, and that the polynomial T^p - T - b is irreducible over k (equivalently, b is not of the form t^p - t for any t in k). Let K be the k-subalgebra of A generated by a. Then K is a field, K/k is a cyclic Galois extension of degree p, and the centralizer C_A(K) is a central simple K-algebra of degree p.
lemma_as_element_centralizer_csa.proof: Let f(T)=T^p-T-b in k[T]. Since a^p-a=b, we have f(a)=0. Consider the k-algebra homomorphism phi:k[T]->A defined by phi(T)=a. Because b in k is central, f(a)=a^p-a-b=0, so f lies in ker(phi). The kernel is a nonzero ideal of the PID k[T], hence ker(phi)=(g) for a monic polynomial g dividing f. By hypothesis f is irreducible, so g is either 1 or f. The possibility g=1 is impossible because phi(1)=1_A != 0. Therefore ker(phi)=(f), and K=k[a] is canonically isomorphic to k[T]/(f). Hence K is a field and [K:k]=p. The derivative f'(T)=-1 is nonzero, so f is separable. For every i in {0,1,...,p-1}, viewed as an element of the prime field F_p contained in k, we have f(a+i)=(a+i)^p-(a+i)-b=(a^p-a-b)+i^p-i=0. Thus all p roots of f are a+i, and they all lie in K. Therefore f splits in K, so K/k is normal. Since K/k is also separable, it is a Galois extension of degree p. The assignment a -> a+1 defines a k-automorphism sigma of K: indeed a+1 is a root of f, so the k-algebra map k[T]->K sending T to a+1 factors through k[T]/(f)=K, and its inverse is given by a -> a-1. For i=0,1,...,p-1, sigma^i(a)=a+i, so the powers sigma^i are distinct; in particular sigma has order p. Since [K:k]=p and K/k is Galois, Gal(K/k) has order p, and sigma generates it. Thus K/k is a cyclic Galois extension of degree p. Finally, A is a central simple k-algebra of degree p^2, and K is a subfield of A of degree p over k. By ref_1, the centralizer C_A(K) is a central simple K-algebra of degree deg(A)/[K:k]=p^2/p=p. This proves the lemma.

lemma_div_p_separable_max_subfield.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p>2 and let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p. Then D contains a maximal subfield L of k-dimension p such that L/k is separable.
lemma_div_p_separable_max_subfield.proof: Let D be a central division k-algebra of degree p. Then dim_k(D)=p^2. By ref_16, every central division k-algebra contains a maximal subfield that is separable over k; hence D contains a maximal subfield L such that L/k is separable. It remains to check that [L:k]=p. Since D is central simple and L is a subfield, ref_1 applies: L is a maximal subfield of D if and only if C_D(L)=L, and C_D(L) is a central simple L-algebra of degree deg(D)/[L:k]. Because L is maximal, C_D(L)=L. As an L-algebra, L has degree 1, so deg(D)/[L:k]=1. Therefore [L:k]=deg(D)=p. Thus L is a maximal subfield of D of k-dimension p and L/k is separable. The assumption char(k)=p>2 is not needed for this argument, but it is satisfied.
